reviews.review: A fun, lighthearted game about shooting giant bugs with insane weaponry. It really shines when playing with a friend.

My first impression of this game is: It looks like Saints Row 1, Saints Row 2 and Saints Row the third for graphics because of havok, some mission is easy for some positions when selected, and needs some tactics and skills when some mission is not good for this position for 100% complication; and this is a funny game of course.
I will make the full review after the story mode completed.
Points: 10/10 and 100/100
[spoiler] And one last thing: EDF!!! [/spoiler]

first, legitimate actual warning: if you have arachnophobia or Bug Phobia In General, do not play this game. 
Do not look at screenshots. In fact, pretend it doesn't exist. 


Otherwise, do you want some absolutely absurd co-op gameplay? one that's fun and has the most ridiculous dialogue ever? well, play this game. It's very silly, very fun co-op. It is also an incredible grind to 100% if you care about that and even more if you want to max out weapons and armor, so just know that going in. However, the game itself is really fun so if you're willing to invest the time, it will reward you.

just uh, don't teamkill your friends as air raider. unless it's hilarious.

This is EDF 4 ported to DX11 with slightly higher graphical fidelity and far less optimization. Almost everything in the game is reused and the few things that aren't reused stand out like a sore thumb. This is a DLC  that they're charging you $60 for. Aside from a slight upscaling in graphics they managed to completely butcher the storyline and absolutely destroy the balancing of the classes with weird new mechanics. Remember your favorite gun? It probably has 10 new annoying mechanics to deal with now like "Loses power the longer it fires + the further you are from the enemy" or imagine charging an assault rifle to 30 bullets, and then not being able to stop firing until all 30 bullets are spent? Need to look around? Hope you don't shoot a teammate. Did you like the dragons in EDF 4? Well they're fat flying frogs now. Yep. Cause that was necessary.

There are some slight QOL improvements such as getting credit for lower-difficulty missions when completing higher difficulty ones as well as friendly AI being more present and more capable when they are present. It's a bit easier to hold onto one weapon before getting its next version due to "star levels", but since they gutted the functionality of most weapons as I described above, you're essentially FORCED into doing this unless you enjoy learning a brand new mechanic that gets in between you and shooting your gun for every single new gun you try. 

EDF5 is fine for someone who has never played an EDF game before, and never plans to play any others. For actual EDF players though, this game is some weird anomaly where nothing works or looks like you'd expect; even though every asset is reused anyway.
